`RoBMA` is a comprehensive R package for Bayesian meta-analysis [@RoBMA].
It provides single-model fits, meta-regression, location-scale model, multilevel models, fully Bayesian model-averaged ensembles, and built-in publication-bias adjustment using selection models, PET-PEESE, and Robust Bayesian Meta-Analysis (RoBMA).
Posterior sampling is performed by JAGS through a custom C++ module that implements the weighted distributions used in selection models.
Prior handling, plotting, and Bayesian diagnostics are delegated to the companion package `BayesTools`.

This vignette gives a high-level map of the package and points to the more detailed vignettes that follow.

## System Requirements

`RoBMA` requires JAGS 4.3.1 or newer [@plummer2003jags].
Install JAGS from <https://mcmc-jags.sourceforge.io/> before installing the R package.

```r
install.packages("RoBMA")
```

**Note on backwards compatibility.**
The 4.0 release is not backwards compatible with earlier versions of the package.
The *Paper Companions* section accompanies the methodological papers in which `RoBMA` was originally developed and illustrated; the vignettes there have been updated to the 4.0 version of the package and the numerical results differ from the published values because the underlying algorithms have changed.
To reproduce the published analyses exactly, install `RoBMA` 3.6.1 together with `BayesTools` 0.2.23:

```r
remotes::install_version("BayesTools", version = "0.2.23")
remotes::install_version("RoBMA",      version = "3.6.1")
```

## Main Functions

The package exposes a small set of high-level fitting functions.

| Function              | What it fits                                                               |
|:----------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`brma()`](../reference/brma.html), [`brma.norm()`](../reference/brma.html) | Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis                                      |
| [`brma.glmm()`](../reference/brma.glmm.html) | Bayesian GLMM meta-analysis (binomial / log OR or Poisson / log IRR)       |
| [`bselmodel()`](../reference/bselmodel.html) | Bayesian weight-function selection model                                   |
| [`bPET()`](../reference/bPET.html), [`bPEESE()`](../reference/bPEESE.html) | Bayesian PET / PEESE publication-bias adjustment                           |
| [`BMA()`](../reference/BMA.html), [`BMA.norm()`](../reference/BMA.html) | Bayesian model-averaging across presence / absence of effect and heterogeneity (no bias adjustment) |
| [`BMA.glmm()`](../reference/BMA.glmm.html) | Bayesian model-averaging for GLMM meta-analysis                            |
| [`RoBMA()`](../reference/RoBMA.html) | Robust Bayesian model-averaging including publication-bias models          |

`brma()` and `RoBMA()` are the main workhorses.
`brma()` fits a single model in the same spirit as `metafor::rma()`; `RoBMA()` averages across an ensemble that includes publication-bias adjustment.
`BMA()` is `RoBMA()` without the bias-adjustment models.

All fitting functions

- share an effect-size interface (`yi`, `sei`/ `vi`, `measure` arguments; apart from glmm),
- can be extended into a meta-regression (`mods` argument),
- can be extended into a location-scale model (`scale` argument),
- can be extended into a multilevel model (`cluster` argument),
- and all produce objects that work with the same set of inference helpers (`summary()`, `plot()`, `predict()`, `loo()`, `funnel()`, `regplot()`, residuals and influence diagnostics, ...).

## Vignette Map

The vignettes are organized into four sections.

### Foundations

| Vignette                  | Topic                                                                 |
|:--------------------------|:----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [*Prior Distributions*](01-prior-distributions.html) | Default, informed, and custom priors; rescaling guidance              |
| [*Bayesian Meta-Analysis*](02-bayesian-meta-analysis.html) | Random-effects meta-analysis with `brma()`, compared with `metafor::rma()` |
| [*Feature Coverage*](03-feature-coverage.html) | Overview of available functionality across model families             |

These three vignettes cover prior specification, a baseline `brma()` workflow, and current feature coverage.
The Bayesian meta-analysis vignette walks through the BCG-vaccine example from `metafor` in `brma()`, covering summaries, meta-regression, marginal means, residuals, influence, LOO, and the standard meta-analytic plots.

### Correspondence with `metafor`

| Vignette                                          | Topic                                                |
|:--------------------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------|
| [*Multilevel Meta-Analysis*](10-metafor-parity-multilevel.html) | `brma()` with `cluster` ↔ `metafor::rma.mv()` for 3-level data |
| [*Publication-Bias Adjustment*](11-metafor-parity-publication-bias.html) | `bselmodel()` / `bPET()` / `bPEESE()` ↔ `metafor::selmodel()` |
| [*Location-Scale Models*](12-metafor-parity-location-scale.html) | `brma()` with `scale` ↔ `metafor::rma.ls()`          |
| [*Generalized Linear Mixed-Effects Meta-Analysis*](13-metafor-parity-glmm.html) | `brma.glmm()` ↔ `metafor::rma.glmm()` for binomial and Poisson outcomes |

Each vignette starts from a `metafor` analysis and shows the matching `RoBMA` syntax, output, and diagnostics.

### Bayesian Model Averaging

| Vignette                       | Topic                                                                  |
|:-------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [*Bayesian Model Averaging*](20-bayesian-model-averaging.html) | Accounting for model uncertainty across presence and absence of effect and heterogeneity, with posterior model probabilities and inclusion Bayes factors |
| [*Robust Bayesian Meta-Analysis*](21-robust-bayesian-meta-analysis.html) | Extending the ensemble to publication-bias models used in `RoBMA()`, with `PSMA`, `PP`, and bespoke ensemble specifications |

The first vignette introduces model averaging on an ensemble of models with and without effect and heterogeneity.
The second extends the ensemble to publication-bias models used in `RoBMA()`.

These vignettes reproduce or update analyses from published papers and serve as references when citing the corresponding methodological work.

## Where to Start

- Curious about Bayesian meta-analysis and already familiar with `metafor`: read *Bayesian Meta-Analysis*, then the *Correspondence with `metafor`* vignettes for the model family you use most.
- First Bayesian meta-analysis: read *Prior Distributions* and then *Bayesian Meta-Analysis*.
- Publication-bias adjustment: read *Robust Bayesian Meta-Analysis*, with *Adjusting for Publication Bias Tutorial* as a worked example.
